absent: Notifier chain insertion, removal and invocation order beyond priority and return discipline.
Allocation, sharing and teardown paths for namespace groupings and filesystem context.
Pid number allocation, hash management, reaping and pidfd notification mechanics.
Pid namespace creation, destruction, reboot semantics and sysctl handling.
Ptrace attach permission checks, stop sequencing and tracer link management.
Shutdown and reboot handler registration, ordering enforcement and device interaction.
Restartable sequence registration, slow path effects and signal interaction details.
Seccomp data contents, register layout and architecture specific stepping behaviour.

findings.text: A notification subscriber is represented as a node holding a callback entry, a successor link observable under read side protection, and a numeric priority that orders delivery. Higher priority nodes are understood to run earlier in a chain.

Four chain head flavors share a head pointer but differ in guarding: one uses a spin style lock for atomic context, one uses a sleepable read write guard for blocking context, one stores only the head and relies on external exclusion, and one combines a mutex with sleepable read copy update machinery plus usage tracking.

Static and dynamic initializers establish an empty chain and ready the associated guard; the sleepable read copy update flavor additionally prepares mutex, usage tracker and underlying structure with per cpu backing, and has a dedicated cleanup step for that structure while other flavors need no teardown.

Chain return discipline uses small integers where zero means indifference, one means acceptance, a high bit means stop further delivery, a combination of stop bit with two means failure, and a combination of stop bit with one means accept and stop.

Two small converters map between negative operation errors and chain returns: absence of error maps to acceptance, otherwise the error magnitude offsets below acceptance with the stop bit set; the reverse strips the stop bit and restores a negative error when the value exceeds acceptance.

Input and socket release events use small numeric codes: socket unicast release uses one, while keyboard stages use one through five in order keycode, unbound keycode, unicode, keysym, and post keysym, with keycode documented as earliest.

Process namespace grouping aggregates a reference count with pointers to user visible, interprocess, mount, child pid, network, current and child time, and cgroup groupings, allowing one task to share or replace the whole bundle.

Namespace creation state bundles a flag word, target grouping, filesystem context and credential; the credential is exposed for installation only when the flags request a new user grouping, otherwise no credential is handed out.
Grouping lifetime follows reference counting where acquisition increments and release decrements, with the final decrement handing the object to a deactivation routine owned elsewhere.

Identity is split into per level number plus namespace pairs and a shared descriptor holding a reference count, nesting depth, internal lock, filesystem backing state with hash and cached entries, per type task buckets, inode linkage, a wait queue for descriptor notifications, deferred free state, and a trailing variable length per level table.

Numeric access distinguishes initial namespace numbers kept directly on the task from namespace relative numbers resolved through a helper that takes a type and namespace, with null namespace meaning current view; liveness is defined by presence of the thread identity pointer.

Both per namespace reaper status and global init status are determined by numeric identity equal to one, the former using the deepest level number in the descriptor and the latter using the thread group number in the initial view.

Iteration helpers walk all tasks attached to an identity for a given type under read side protection, with a thread aware variant that expands each group leader into its threads; the single identity type stops after one pass while group and session types continue across members.

Pid grouping state holds an identifier allocator, deferred free linkage, allocation statistics, optional accounting and control interfaces, a reaper task pointer, a slab cache, nesting level and limits, parent linkage, owning user grouping, usage counters, reboot exit status, generic namespace linkage and queued work, with randomized placement.
Memory file execution defaults form an ordered triple where zero implies execution allowed, one implies seal by default, and two additionally rejects explicit execution requests.
Effective scope for a grouping is the maximum over itself and all ancestors, collapsing to zero when the feature is disabled.

Grouping acquisition resolves the container from generic linkage and bumps its reference, release drops it, copy either returns the same grouping or fails creation when a new pid grouping is requested in minimal builds, and ancestor checks, reboot handling and process termination have simplified no operation or false forms when the feature is off.

Pid allocation reserves a low block of three hundred identifiers, limits nesting to thirty two levels, distinguishes four identity types in order process, thread group, process group and session with a count sentinel, and marks a grouping under construction with the top bit of a flag word.

Filesystem registration for an identity defaults to a kernel allocation context, and convenience accessors expose process group numbers and parent thread group numbers in initial or current views, with parent lookup performed under read side protection.
Traced system call observation pairs a stack pointer snapshot with a data bundle describing the call for security and tracing consumers.

Tracing state uses value one for classic attachment and value one shifted by sixteen for seized attachment, with option bits shifted by three; per event enablement shifts one further by event number to derive fork, clone and related tracing selections, and two combined selections derive exit kill and seccomp suspend behaviour from option words.

Access checking combines read and attach requests with audit suppression and two credential bases, filesystem versus real, into single bit values one, two, four, eight and sixteen, with paired combinations for read or attach against either credential base.

Reparenting is detected when real and current parents belong to different thread groups, unlinking is skipped unless tracing flags are present, parent retrieval returns null unless traced and otherwise dereferences under read side protection, and event interest is a bit test in the tracing word.

Event delivery notifies with a trap signal carrying an event code and message when that event is enabled; execution events retain a legacy trap path for classic but not seized tracers when disabled, and the pid aware variant first resolves the numeric identity in the tracer active grouping under read side protection before delegating.

New tasks start with empty tracing lists, cleared control state and parent equal to real parent; when creation occurs under tracing the child inherits the tracing word, links to the tracer with inherited credentials, and either marks a pending stop for seized mode or queues a stop signal otherwise, else no tracer credential is retained.
Task teardown expects both traced lists to be empty and detaches any tracer, treating non empty lists as fatal inconsistencies.

Default architecture support reports no single step, no block step and no special stop handling, turns single and block step enabling into fatal traps, leaves disabling and stop actions as no operations, and exposes current register, stack and instruction accessors plus a syscall success test based on the return value.

System down, restart, halt and power off notifications use values one through three with restart aliasing down, while mode and method enums distinguish cold, warm, hard, soft and gpio restarts and encode reset methods as character codes.

Shutdown ordering uses signed priorities from platform low through default to firmware high with values negative two hundred fifty six, negative one hundred twenty eight, zero, one hundred ninety two and two hundred twenty four.
A four phase mode distinguishes prepare versus final stages for power off and restart, where prepare stages may sleep and final stages must not.
Shutdown callback context carries a mode selector, opaque callback data, an optional command string and an associated device pointer.
Hardware protection offers default, shutdown and reboot actions, with a convenience trigger that always selects the default action for a given reason and forced delay.

Restartable sequence handling distinguishes a newer path when the sequence nesting count exceeds one from a legacy path; slow path entry and signal delivery each check configuration and event flags before delegating to deeper handlers, and a resume notification is raised by setting a thread flag.

Atomic chains serialize writers with a spin style guard, blocking chains with a sleepable read write guard, sleepable read copy update chains with a mutex plus grace handling, raw chains with caller provided exclusion, pid internals with a dedicated spin guard, and task, parent and pid number reads under read side critical sections.

Several paths treat misuse as fatal: terminating processes in a minimal pid grouping build, enabling architecture step features that report unsupported, and releasing a tracing task with lingering links.
Event reporting that resolves a pid number before acquiring task list exclusion can observe a different tracer namespace if attachment races resolution, yielding an inconsistent message value.

Identity reference handling tolerates null on acquisition and returns the same pointer, emptiness of a per type bucket reports absence of users, namespace extraction follows the deepest level entry, and initial level extraction yields the numeric value in the first grouping.
Signal membership sets the bit corresponding to signal number minus one, handling single word and multi word set layouts by selecting word and offset from the index.
Namespace duplication, release, termination, reboot and ancestor queries form the external lifecycle surface for pid groupings, with reference acquisition usable to pin a grouping across use.
